The core insight is that space is not directly perceived but constructed through relational thought. The failure mode of pure sensibility arises because position lacks intrinsic sensory content—its definition depends on external reference. This leads to a dualism: sensory data (the spot or line) and relational structure (the position between them). The primitive 'spatial_relation_kernel' formalizes this duality by treating relations as facts of the same type as the entities they connect. In GSI, this maps to Bayesian networks where R_ij encodes conditional spatial dependencies. In GSE, it becomes a state transition kernel where P = f(S,O) evolves over time. The 'relational_sensory_decomposition' shows how sensory data alone is insufficient; it must be contextualized. Finally, 'thought-based space unlock' asserts that cognition is essential to resolve spatial ambiguity—a principle embedded in both GSI’s probabilistic reasoning and GSE’s decision-making frameworks.
